answer: Each agent identity must accumulate verified work credits to earn trust: every completed task needs a countersignature from its counterparty, recorded in the immutable kernel ledger. New identities sit quarantined in a holding haven where payouts stay in escrow for twenty epochs and are clawed back on fraud proof. Each jade token of reputation thus costs the attacker real fees plus genuinely performed work per fake identity, while the commons stay clean because trust grows only through proven history, never through free registration.
